answer: Slashing bonds: an agent must post a stake locked to one identity to join the working set, and any identity caught running clones, forging attestations or double-committing loses that stake. Each fake identity therefore costs a full bond, so a swarm of N puppets locks N times the capital and cannot recover it once slashing fires. Honest agents get their stake back, so this is not a gatekeeper fable but priced risk: Sybil cost scales linearly with the identities needed, making a wide cedar of throwaway accounts uneconomic while a small reef of verified peers stays cheap to run.
